why_here.Home valley: a sheltered basin where the Sleepwater leaves the uplands: water, a mill head, flat ground, hills on three sides
why_here.the Frostline: a glacier's cirque above the valley: the Sleepwater's source, a tarn, snow late into summer
why_here.Driftwood: the cove at the Sleepwater's mouth, sheltered by the Headland: the valley's landing place
why_here.Fernhollow: timber in the wet woods of the Fern hills, the valley's east wall
why_here.Cogsworth: coal and iron in the coal hills, the fast Cog for power (the Millrace), and the valley floor for a railway out
why_here.Lullford: the lowest place the Lull can be bridged: gravel terraces narrow the floodplain and an island takes the piers
why_here.Gullwick: a cove on the open coast west of the delta: fish, and a beach to haul boats
why_here.Neon Harbour: a deep, sheltered ria clear of the Lull's silt; the falls gave the first crossing, the head of navigation and mill power
why_here.Launch Cape: an exposed headland past the city: rockets go up over open sea, away from people
why_here.Palm Spring: the Willow Run sinks into the gravel and comes up again here: the first water in the dry country
why_here.Dust Gulch: where the Amber leaves the mountains: water, the mine above, the railhead
why_here.the Lode: iron and copper in the massif foothills, reached by a mule track
why_here.Hearthold: a rock between two lava flows below the crater: the only defensible ground on the volcano's seaward side
why_here.Ember forge: the crater's heat at the caldera lip; ore comes down from the Lode by cart
why_here.Cinder Springs: hot springs where the sea seeps into the volcano's warm flank
why_here.Cinderwick: a black-sand cove between the flows: charcoal and fish
why_here.Lagoon Landing: the main isle's lagoon: a drowned crater of the old arc, sheltered water

Lullford Bridge: old stone arches resting on a river island, with an iron swing span for the barges (W7)
Narrows Viaduct: the railway (now the maglev) on tall piers over the gorge
Harbour Bridge: two high arches across the ria, resting on Chapel Islet; tall enough for masts

new_routes.Heather Way: the circle's own road west: from the woodland's glade over the Brackens' moor top, past the Heather crater and the drove well, down to the Brackens gap; closes a loop with the Drover's Road

new_routes.Fern Lane: Fernhollow straight down to the Lull Road: a shortcut that closes the Foothill Road and the Lull Road into a loop
new_routes.Gull Lane: the Lull Road down to Gullwick: a loop with the Coast Path, and Gullwick no longer a dead end off one path
